events.title: Python 2.7 released
events.summary: [Python] 2.7 shipped on July 3, 2010 as the final major release of the [Python] 2 line — bridging users toward [Python] 3 with years of extended support.
events.about: [Python] 2.7 added ordered dictionaries, argparse, and unittest improvements while keeping 2.x compatibility. It became the longest-supported [Python] release — powering legacy systems until the 2020 end-of-life forced the [Python] 3 migration.

narrative.whyChosen: [Python] 2.7 was the last stop before the great [Python] 2→3 migration.
narrative.whyImportant: Extended support kept enterprises on a stable 2.x while libraries ported to 3.
narrative.problemSolved: Teams needed a mature 2.x with modern stdlib pieces while planning [Python] 3 adoption.

events.title: Haskell 2010 language standard published
events.summary: The Haskell 2010 report was finalized in July 2010 — defining the stable language revision used by GHC and textbooks for a decade.
events.about: Haskell 2010 streamlined the language after Haskell 98: foreign function interface support, exceptions, and deprecations that cleaned up corner cases. It became the baseline for learning [functional programming] and for GHC's default language mode.

narrative.whyChosen: Haskell 2010 is the standard revision most Haskell courses and books still reference.
narrative.whyImportant: A stable standard let the ecosystem grow libraries without dialect fragmentation.
narrative.problemSolved: Haskell 98 was too minimal for real systems programming and FFI needs.
